guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: The 81st edition of La Vuelta starts in Monaco, home to a historic Gran Salida. As the Principality becomes the first city to have hosted the start of the three Grand Tours, powerhouses gear for a spectacular first battle. guideposts.label: Welcome to Monaco
guideposts.detail: For the seventh time in 81 editions, and the fourth time in five years, La Vuelta is setting off from outside Spain. After Lisbon (1997 and 2024), Assen (2009), Nîmes (2017), Utrecht (2022) and Piemonte (2025), it is now Monaco’s turn. guideposts.label: A very special day for Langellotti
guideposts.detail: The start in Monaco features a very special participant: Monegasque rider Victor Langelloti (XDS Astana), the only rider from the Principality in the current professional peloton, who will begin his third appearance in La Vuelta on home soil. “As a Monegasque, it is an honour to be able to ride La Vuelta at home and a source of pride to be able to wear this jersey”, says Langellotti, who won both

guideposts.label: Many local figures: Pogacar, Carapaz, Pedersen…
guideposts.detail: Although Langelloti is the only rider from Monaco in the current professional peloton, there are many cyclists who are normally based in the Principality, and several of them will be taking part in this opening time trial. guideposts.label: From Uriarte to Roglic
guideposts.detail: The opening ITT of La Vuelta 26 is the perfect occasion to get familiar with the field of this 81st edition and see who will bring the race to life en route to Granada. Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) is set to be the first rider on course, from 16:17, as he participates in his first Grand Tour. guideposts.label: The 36th edition of La Vuelta to begin with an ITT
guideposts.detail: Today marks the 36th time La Vuelta starts with an ITT (in 81 editions). On the first occasion, in 1948, Bernardo Ruiz and Julian Berrendero were tied after the opening ITT in Madrid. More recently, Brandon McNulty took the first La Roja through an ITT in Lisbon in 2024, three years after Primoz Roglic dominated the opening ITT in Burgos. guideposts.label: Kaden Groves begins his 4th La Vuelta
guideposts.detail: Winner of the points standings in 2023 and 2024, the Australian versatile sprinter has won stages in each of his previous participations: - in Cabo de Gata (stage 11) in 2022 - in Tarragona (4), Borriana (5), and Madrid (21) in 2023 - in Ourem (2), Villablino (14), and Santander (17) in 2024 He also won the points standings 2023 and 2024.

guideposts.label: Kuss starts his third Grand Tour of the year
guideposts.detail: The USA climber was 13th in the Giro d’Italia, where he accompanied Jonas Vingegaard to the overall victory, and 13th in the Tour de France, where he won the opening TTT with Visma-Lease a Bike and animated the two days finishing at Alpe d’Huez (4th on stage 19, 3rd the next day). guideposts.label: The youngest participant in La Vuelta 26 followed by Onley
guideposts.detail: Born in 2006, Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) is the youngest rider at the start of the 81st La Vuelta. He is 20 years and 154 days old today, four months younger than Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché). guideposts.label: Can Küng win the opening ITT of La Vuelta?
guideposts.detail: The Swiss powerhouse, starting at 18:17, is one of two riders to have already won a La Vuelta ITT. It was on the last day of the 2024 edition, in Madrid. Primoz Roglic won the opening and the closing ITTs of the 2021 edition, as well as stage 10 in 2019 and stage 13 in 2020.

guideposts.label: Jay Vine’s sixth La Vuelta
guideposts.detail: The Australian star built a very special relationship with La Vuelta over the years. Back in 2021, it was his first Grand Tour and he most notably impressed with a 3rd place at Pico Villuercas despite crashing on that day due to a mishap with his team car. guideposts.label: Langellotti starts at home
guideposts.detail: Victor Langellotti is the local rider of the Gran Salida, and the only Monegasque rider in the current professional peloton. This is his third La Vuelta after he participated in 2022 with Burgos-BH and in 2025 with Ineos. guideposts.label: Tarling sets off
guideposts.detail: The British powerhouse might be the purest TT talent starting La Vuelta 26. At 22 years old, he’s already won the national and continental titles, as well as a Grand Tour stage (in the Giro 2025), and stood on the podium of the Worlds (3rd in 2023) in addition to his success on the track.
